edition.tagline: One dollar bet. One very big swap.
edition.cue: Serve the mains during the New Year's Eve train party.

s.note: Almond-stuffed prunes wrapped in crisp streaky bacon.
s.how: Push an almond into each of 20 pitted prunes. Wrap each in half a rasher of streaky bacon, using 10 rashers, and secure with a toothpick. Bake at 200C for 15 minutes until the bacon is crisp. Serve warm.

s.note: Icy orange juice slush with a splash of vodka.
s.how: Blend 500ml orange juice with 2 cups ice and 80ml vodka until slushy. Pour into shot glasses and serve straight away, before the market closes. Leave out the vodka for anyone not drinking.

m.note: Slow-roasted rib roast with jus, horseradish cream and potatoes.
m.how: Salt a 2kg standing rib roast the day before and leave uncovered in the fridge. Roast at 120C until 52C inside, about 2.5 hours, rest 30 minutes, then blast at 260C for 8 minutes for a crust. Simmer the pan juices with 300ml beef stock for jus. Serve with 150g horseradish cream and 1kg roast potatoes.

w.note: Orange butter cake soaked in a sticky orange glaze.
w.how: Beat 200g butter, 200g caster sugar and the zest of 2 oranges, add 3 eggs and fold in 250g self-raising flour with 100ml orange juice. Bake in a lined tin at 170C for 45 minutes. Boil 100ml orange juice concentrate with 50g sugar for 3 minutes and brush over the warm cake.

d.note: Fresh orange juice and chilled sparkling wine in flutes.
d.how: Squeeze 4 oranges, about 300ml juice, and chill well. Fill four flutes halfway with the juice and gently top with chilled sparkling wine, about 300ml in total, pouring slowly so it does not foam over.
